sentences.text: Solicitor Priya Shah attended the meeting with client Leanne Carter to take instructions regarding protection from ex-partner Ryan Hale.
Client Leanne Carter described being in a relationship with Ryan Hale for six years, which ended in August.
Ryan Hale moved out to his brother's residence after the split.
Leanne Carter remains at 9 Calder Court, which is her tenancy in her name.
Client has a daughter, Mia, who is four years old and currently at nursery.
Ryan Hale is Mia's father; he was seeing her on Sundays until October, after which Leanne stopped it.
Ryan Hale has been visiting the flat every weekend since August, including Friday or Saturday nights, by knocking and shouting through the letterbox.
On the 12th of October, Ryan Hale put his hands around Leanne's neck in the hallway while she opened the door to give Mia's bag, causing her to be unable to breathe for a period.
Mia was asleep in her room during the incident on the 12th of October.
Leanne's neighbour called the police after hearing her screaming during the incident on the 12th of October, and Ryan Hale was arrested.
Leanne has a crime reference number for the incident on the 12th of October, which is H R one four.
Ryan Hale was released on bail after the 12th of October, but the bail expired and he is currently under investigation with no current bail conditions.
Leanne visited her GP two days after the 12th of October, and the GP recorded marks on her neck.
On the 20th of October, Ryan Hale arrived again and smashed Leanne's phone, which she had to replace at a cost of about two hundred pounds.
Leanne reported the phone-smashing incident to the officer on the case.
On the 3rd of November, Ryan Hale sent a text message to Leanne threatening to kill her, which she has screenshot and also has voice notes saying 'I'll regret it'.
Leanne's friend Gemma told her that Ryan Hale keeps a knife in his van for work, though Leanne has never seen it personally.
Ryan Hale has parental responsibility for Mia as he is listed on the birth certificate.
Leanne is employed part-time at a pharmacy for about eighteen hours per week and receives universal credit.
Leanne qualifies for legal aid due to police and GP evidence of abuse and will need to provide three months' bank statements and a universal credit statement.
Client's primary objective is for Ryan Hale to stop coming to the flat and stop messaging her.
Leanne wants Mia to not see Ryan Hale until the situation is resolved.
Solicitor advised that a non-molestation order should be applied for to prevent Ryan Hale from contacting Leanne, using or threatening violence, and coming within a set distance of
The non-molestation order can be made without notice to Ryan Hale due to the history of strangulation and threats to kill, allowing him to respond at a return hearing.
Breaching a non-molestation order is a criminal offence, and Leanne should call the police immediately if Ryan Hale breaks it.
The non-molestation order would not prevent Ryan Hale from applying for contact with Mia, but any contact would be dealt with separately and the court would be aware of the abuse.
Client will email the solicitor the crime reference number (H R one four), screenshots, and voice notes by Wednesday the 25th.
Client will provide three months' bank statements and universal credit statement by Wednesday the 25th.
Solicitor will complete the legal aid application today and draft the witness statement to send to client by Friday the 27th.
Solicitor will aim to file the non-molestation order application on Monday the 30th.
